_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory hairy cell leukemia (HCL) who received at least two prior systemic therapies, including treatment with a purine nucleoside analog (PNA)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 1053 (CD-ON-CAT-8015-1053), "A Pivotal Multicenter Trial of Moxetumomab Pasudotox in Relapsed/Refractory Hairy Cell Leukemia"
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with relapsed or refractory HCL who had received at least 2 prior systemic therapies including a purine nucleoside analog (PNA); heavily pretreated, median 3 prior therapies (range 2-11), median age 60 years
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Rate of durable complete response (CR) per blinded independent central review (BICR), defined as CR followed by hematologic remission maintained for more than 180 days
pivotal_trials.result: IRC-assessed durable CR rate 30% (24/80; 95% CI: 20, 41); ORR 75% (95% CI: 64, 84); CR 41% (95% CI: 30, 53); median duration of response not reached

key_safety: Most common (≥20%) non-laboratory adverse reactions: infusion related reactions, edema, nausea, fatigue, headache, pyrexia, constipation, anemia, diarrhea. Boxed warning toxicities: capillary leak syndrome (CLS) in 34% (44/129) and hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) in 7% (9/129). Discontinuations for AEs in 15% (12/80), most commonly HUS (5%).
target_moa: CD22-directed cytotoxin: an anti-CD22 antibody fragment fused to truncated Pseudomonas exotoxin PE38; binds CD22 on B cells, is internalized, and causes ADP-ribosylation of eukaryotic elongation factor 2, inhibiting protein synthesis and causing apoptotic cell death
modality: Immunotoxin (recombinant CD22-directed antibody-fragment/Pseudomonas exotoxin fusion cytotoxin) — other

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for Capillary Leak Syndrome (CLS) and Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS), including life-threatening cases; delay dosing or discontinue as recommended, and discontinue LUMOXITI in patients with HUS

rems.type: The Division of Risk Management agreed that a REMS is not needed to ensure the benefits of moxetumomab pasudotox exceed its risk

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee nor any other external consultants

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted for treatment of HCL (originally CD22-positive HCL)

summary.text: LUMOXITI received regular (traditional) approval under a Priority review BLA supported by orphan drug and Fast Track designations; it was granted Fast Track on January 26, 2018 with a rolling submission, and orphan designation for HCL. Approval was based on the single-arm pivotal Phase 3 Study 1053; it was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: The review team recommends regular approval of moxetumomab pasudotox for the following indication
On January 26, 2018, moxetumomab pasudotox was granted Fast Track designation and permission to proceed with rolling submission.
The Applicant was granted Orphan Designation for moxetumomab pasudotox for the treatment of patients with HCL and is therefore exempt from pediatric studies under the Pediatric Research Equity Act.

requirement.text: PMR 3477-1: Conduct a study characterizing the safety of moxetumomab pasudotox in patients 65 years of age and older and in patients with moderate renal impairment, with interim and final reports and data collection 2 years and 5 years post-approval respectively

citations.quote: PMR 3477-1 Conduct a study to provide evidence characterizing 1) the safety of moxetumomab pasudotox in patient who are 65 years of age and older and 2) the safety of moxetumomab pasudotox in patients who have moderate renal impairment.
